rows.name: an agent on it calls OpenRouter's Chat Completions with the 1017 id and the reasoning it asks for
a definition's language: its agents inherit it, an agent's own stays when it is applied, and a run takes its own or the definition's
the TypeScript SDK sends language when it makes, configures and runs agents
an agent's language: in its prompt once and the same every turn, shown, changed and cleared by PATCH, refused when junk
existing agents recover from static fallback on their next call; tenant and scope keys never exchange
agents can live until deleted, or for a chosen time
models are chosen by name over REST, at creation and mid-conversation
an azure model without a deployment, a refused key, a missing deployment and a rate limit each end the run with Azure's reason
Azure Flash uses platform credentials and catalog billing and replays reasoning with tool results
a tenant on the platform's keys runs azure models the platform deploys, through the deployment, billed at the catalog's price
an agent with no key for the fallback's provider ends as the content filter ended it
billing: the blocked Azure call is the platform's cost, recorded but never charged; the account pays once, for the fallback's answer
a response Azure's content filter blocks is asked once more on OpenRouter's DeepSeek, leaving only the answer in history
Pi's compaction summaries carry the agent's data policy too
agents, runs, definitions and configure: data_collection deny sent when set, on Chat Completions and Responses; nothing by default
if DeepSeek's endpoint refuses anyway, the same request is asked again: no host kept off, no order
DeepSeek's refusal as OpenRouter's Chat Completions gives it (127 characters) is classed and retried as it was; the answer names its host
a multi-turn tool conversation, then a turn on DeepSeek's own endpoint: never refused
an agent that names no model gets the first default its tenant or key scope has a key for, and /v1/me says which
a tenant's own key comes before the platform's: only an Anthropic key is Sonnet 5.5 on it, never DeepSeek on the platform's credit
the default is for agents being made: an upsert or a definition applied that names no model leaves an existing agent's
a Codex model on a tenant's endpoint gets the ChatGPT backend's own request, with a placeholder account for the endpoint to replace
an Anthropic model on a tenant's endpoint gets Anthropic's own request, signatures included, with identity tokens and at no token cost
a tenant endpoint's errors end the turn with its message, without retries
OpenRouter models on a tenant's endpoint use its Responses API, reasoning carried back, and compact through it
a Bedrock model on a tenant's endpoint gets Converse's own request at its region's path, unsigned, with its signatures sent back
a tenant cannot give its agent a model object: a free copy of a catalog model on the platform's key is refused
on a platform key a response is billed at the catalog's price, whatever the agent's stored model says, and one without usage is charged an estimate
an unbilled admin tenant's responses on platform or admin keys are as the provider reported them, never estimated
a definition's maxOutputTokens and temperature: its agents take them, an agent's own stay when it is applied, and a stateless run takes them too
the TypeScript SDK sends maxOutputTokens and temperature when it makes, configures and runs agents
an agent's maxOutputTokens and temperature go on its model calls, are refused where its model takes none, and stay its own
an agent's calls send their model's hosts: V4.1 Flash five, 1017 two ignored with at most 131,072 tokens; nothing else
1017:nitro resolves as 1017 does (catalog, price, 131,072, Chat Completions, no hosts, two ignored) and is sent with its variant
1017:morph is 1017 served by Morph alone: sent as 1017 with provider.only morph, priced and resolved as 1017
over the API: the lookup's price reaches an end user's hold, so a dear model is refused where the mid-range price would have started
over the API: an agent keeps what the lookup said, a move looks up too, and its calls name the id and add no routing
a model that always reasons is called with its least reasoning when an agent asks for none, and as asked otherwise
a run whose first model call is refused fails with the provider's error, on every API, before its stream or in it
a structured run forces final_output from the first request when it is the model's only tool, and on the reminder when it has others
a provider that refuses a forced tool_choice is asked again without it; forcing stops after three requests
codeMode: false leaves out codemode and the runtime's code rules; with no tools at all, the prompt is the instructions and the sender note
a prompt with output ends on a final_output call that fits its schema, which the outcome returns
a structured run the model ends in text is reminded once, then fails with output_missing; a prompt without output takes the tool away
output is refused unless it is a schema for an object, on a prompt that starts its own turn
the SDK's run() takes a zod, TypeBox or JSON schema for output and types run.output by it
GET /v1/models carries toolCallStreaming; a model on an operator's endpoint has its upstream model's
an agent naming no model stores the alias; Particle's outage moves that call to 1017, with history, routing and records on the model that ran
a request the model would refuse anywhere does not move; a real model never moves
a tenant with no OpenRouter key falls to what it holds; an upsert keeps the alias, and naming a model leaves it
over the API: Particle's failed attempt releases its end user's hold and costs nothing; only the model that answered is charged
